facts.text: Japan: a complete school lunch has a staple food (rice or bread), a main dish, a side dish, and a carton of milk.
Japan: nearly all students eat lunch in their own classrooms; very few elementary or junior high schools have a cafeteria.
Japan: students take turns on serving and cleanup duty, and they wear caps and white aprons while serving.
Japan: before eating, the class says itadakimasu together to give thanks, and after the meal they say gochisosama.
Japan: school lunch is treated as part of education, called shokuiku, or food education; menus are often planned by nutritionists and meals are usually cooked from scratch.
Japan: the School Lunch Law of 1954 made school lunches a nationwide program.
France: a school lunch includes a main dish, a side dish, a dairy product, and a starter and/or a dessert.
France: the town is in charge of the school canteen menu, and menus are usually posted on the town's website.
France: a school lunch must last at least 30 minutes, not counting time spent waiting in line.
France: water and bread must be freely available at school lunch.
France: the town sets the price of school lunches and may base it on how much the family earns.
France: since 1 November 2019, every school canteen must serve a vegetarian menu at least once a week; it may include eggs or dairy products.
United States: the National School Lunch Program was set up by the National School Lunch Act, which President Harry Truman signed in 1946.
United States: the program gives balanced lunches to children each school day, either at low cost or free.
United States: school lunches are built from five food groups: fruits, vegetables, grains, meat or other protein foods, and milk.
United States: children from families with low incomes can get the lunch free or at a reduced price; other students pay a low full price.
United States: students get school lunch by joining the lunch line in the school cafeteria.
Taiwan: the school lunch program has been running since 1982.
Taiwan: a typical school lunch has rice, vegetables, meat, soup, and fruit.
Taiwan: in many schools, students serve lunch to each other and eat it in their classrooms.

facts.text: Taiwan: the Ministry of Education sets nutrition standards for school lunches and runs a website where anyone can see each school's daily menu.
Taiwan: several cities, including Taipei, Taoyuan, Taichung, and Kaohsiung, give free lunches to students at public elementary and junior high schools, most of them starting in 2026.
